title: 10 Best Email Warmup Service Providers for B2B Outreach in 2026
excerpt: Discover the 10 best email warmup services for B2B outreach in 2026. Compare features, use cases, and find the right email warmup tool for your business.
introduction: For B2B sales teams, sending cold emails is only effective when those emails actually reach the prospect’s inbox. A strong subject line or well-written sales pitch won’t help much if your messages consistently end up in spam. This is where email warmup services can play an important role. Email warmup is the process of gradually building sending activity and establishing a healthy reputation for a new, inactive, or recently configured mailbox before increasing outbound email volume. An email warmup service can automate much of this process, making it easier for sales teams and agencies to prepare multiple inboxes for outreach. However, not every warmup platform works in the same way. Some focus mainly on automated warmup, while others combine warmup with inbox placement testing, deliverability monitoring, or cold email automation. In this guide, we compare the 10 best email warmup service providers for B2B outreach in 2026, along with their key strengths and the type of business they are best suited for.

sections.title: What Is Email Warmup?
paragraphs: Email warmup is the process of gradually establishing sending activity for a new or inactive email mailbox or domain before using it for larger-scale outreach.

A mailbox with little or no sending history does not have the same reputation as an established business mailbox. Sending a large number of emails immediately can create unnecessary deliverability risks.
An email warm up tool automates some of this activity by creating controlled email interactions and gradually increasing sending activity. Depending on the platform, additional features may include:
Automated warmup
Sending-volume controls
Inbox placement testing
Spam monitoring
Domain reputation monitoring
Blacklist checks
Deliverability reports
Mailbox health monitoring

However, warmup should not be considered a guarantee of inbox placement. Email providers also evaluate authentication, recipient engagement, spam complaints, sending behavior, and other reputation signals.

sections.title: How Does an Email Warm Up Tool Work?
paragraphs: An email warm up tool automates the process of gradually building sending activity for a new or inactive mailbox. The basic process typically involves:
Connect your mailbox, Link your Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or other supported email account.
Start with controlled activity, The tool begins with a lower level of email activity.
Increase activity gradually, Sending activity is adjusted progressively rather than increasing suddenly.
Monitor deliverability, Depending on the platform, you can monitor mailbox health, spam placement, and other deliverability signals.
Begin real outreach, Once your setup is ready, introduce your B2B campaigns gradually rather than immediately sending at high volume.

sections.title: What to Look for in an Email Warmup Service
paragraphs: Choosing an email warmup service based only on price isn’t enough. Before selecting a provider, consider these factors:
Email Provider Support: Make sure it supports your provider, such as Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
Warmup Controls: Check whether you can control sending activity and warmup settings.
Deliverability Monitoring: Look for tools that help monitor mailbox health and deliverability.
Inbox Placement Testing: Testing can help you understand where emails are landing across different providers.
Scalability: If you’re managing multiple inboxes, choose a platform that can grow with your outreach needs.
Security: Review the permissions required before connecting your business email account.
Integrations: Check whether the service works smoothly with your existing cold email or sales engagement tools.

sections.title: Common Email Warmup Mistakes to Avoid
paragraphs: Using an email warmup service doesn’t automatically make an outreach campaign deliverable. Businesses can still encounter problems if they use poor sending practices.
Sending Too Much Too Quickly, Avoid making a sudden jump from minimal activity to a large outbound campaign.
Ignoring Email Authentication, Make sure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are properly configured for your domain.
Using Poor-Quality Email Lists, Invalid or outdated email addresses can increase bounce rates and negatively affect campaign performance.
Treating Warmup as a Guarantee, Warmup does not guarantee that every email will reach the inbox. Mailbox providers consider multiple reputation and engagement signals.
Ignoring Recipient Feedback, If recipients frequently report messages as spam or show little engagement, reassess your targeting, messaging, and sending practices.
Scaling Without Monitoring, Don’t increase email volume simply because a warmup period has ended. Monitor your actual campaign performance and deliverability signals as you scale
